title: Arthritis Exercise App — Deep Research Report

sections.title: Existing Arthritis Exercise Apps
sections.content:
The market splits into two tiers: enterprise MSK platforms (employer/insurance-funded) and consumer apps (direct-to-user). Enterprise platforms dominate in funding and clinical validation but are inaccessible to most individuals.

**Enterprise MSK Platforms (B2B2C — employer/insurer-funded):**

• Hinge Health — Market leader, $588M revenue in 2025, projecting $732M in 2026. Offers PT-designed exercise programs, FDA-cleared wearable pain relief device, 1-on-1 coaching. Zero cost to members through employers. 20M eligible lives, 97% client retention. Delivers 2.4x ROI for employers. Recently filed S-1 for IPO.

• Sword Health — $3B valuation, $340M total funding. AI-powered virtual PT with motion tracking sensors. Acquired Kaia Health for $285M in January 2026, expanding to 100M eligible people. Covers back, hip, knee, neck, shoulder, hand, wrist, elbow, ankle, and foot conditions.

• Kaia Health (now Sword) — Pioneered smartphone-based pose estimation for exercise form correction via Motion Coach. Clinically validated AI motion analysis provides real-time audiovisual feedback comparable to trained physiotherapists. No additional hardware needed. 10-15 minute exercise sessions with dedicated health coach.

**Consumer/Direct-to-Patient Apps:**

• Jointfully Osteoarthritis — Top-rated arthritis app (5/5 on both iOS and Android). Includes PT exercise tutorials, activity goal tracking, medication/weight/mood/pain logging, daily tips, and doctor-shareable progress reports. Free with premium tier.

• MyRA (My Rheumatoid Arthritis) — RA-specific symptom tracker with sliding-scale pain tracking across daily activities (morning mobility, cooking, etc.), custom notes, voice memos, photos, and visual disease state timeline. Generates summary reports for doctor visits. Limitation: no direct provider sharing.

• Arthritis Foundation YES Tool — Customized exercise modifications based on arthritis pain level, fitness level, and favorite activities. Free, web and mobile.

• Walk with Ease (Arthritis Foundation) — 16 online exercise videos, walking goal setting, Fitbit integration, progress tracking. Free.

• Pathways Pain Relief — Highly rated on App Store. Brain-retraining approach using diaphragmatic breathing, visualizations, and stress reduction. Not exercise-focused.

• Arthritis Physio — Android-only. OA information and comprehensive exercise library. Free.

**What's Missing Across the Board:**

Enterprise platforms (Hinge, Sword) are clinically excellent but require employer sponsorship — individuals can't self-pay. Consumer apps have poor exercise guidance (mostly static images/text), no form correction, no pose estimation, minimal personalization by joint or arthritis type, and weak progress analytics. No app effectively bridges the gap: clinical-quality exercise guidance accessible to self-paying individuals. The Arthritis Foundation tools are free but basic. There is no standout consumer app that combines video-guided exercises, real-time form feedback, pain tracking, and personalization by specific joints affected.
highlights: Hinge Health: $732M projected 2026 revenue, 20M eligible lives — but employer-only access
Sword Health acquired Kaia Health for $285M (Jan 2026), reaching 100M eligible people
Kaia's Motion Coach proved smartphone pose estimation matches physiotherapist feedback
Jointfully is top-rated consumer app (5/5) but lacks video guidance and form correction
Critical gap: no consumer app offers clinical-quality exercise guidance for self-paying individuals
No app effectively personalizes by specific joints affected and arthritis type

sections.title: Physical Therapy Exercises for Arthritis — Evidence Base
sections.content:
Exercise is first-line treatment for arthritis, supported by high-quality evidence from Cochrane reviews, the ACR, and the Arthritis Foundation. The research is unambiguous: structured exercise significantly reduces pain and improves function.

**ACR 2022 Guidelines (most current)** strongly recommend exercise for OA of hip, knee, and hand, as well as rheumatoid arthritis and juvenile idiopathic arthritis. Exercise is conditionally recommended over pharmacological intervention as initial treatment.

**Four Core Exercise Categories:**

1. Range of Motion (ROM) — Gentle stretching and movements through full joint span. Critical for maintaining/improving joint flexibility. Examples: shoulder circles, wrist flexion/extension, ankle pumps, finger spreads, neck rotation. Should be done daily, especially in the morning to combat stiffness.

2. Strengthening — Building muscle to support and protect joints, reduce stress on them. Quadriceps strengthening shows pooled effect size of 0.32 for both pain reduction and function improvement (95% CI 0.23-0.42). Examples: wall sits, leg lifts, resistance band exercises, grip strengthening, isometric holds. 2-3 times per week.

3. Aerobic/Endurance — Improves cardiovascular health, aids weight control (critical for load-bearing joints), reduces fatigue. Walking, swimming, cycling recommended. 150 minutes/week moderate intensity per ACR guidelines.

4. Aquatic Exercise — Water-based exercise particularly effective for arthritis due to buoyancy reducing joint stress while providing resistance. Strong evidence for both OA and RA. Warm water (92-96°F) adds therapeutic benefit.

**Additional Recommended Modalities:**
• Tai Chi — Strongly recommended by ACR for knee/hip OA. Improves balance, reduces falls risk.
• Yoga — Gentle/chair yoga improves flexibility, reduces pain. Especially beneficial for hand and wrist arthritis.
• Balance training — Critical for fall prevention in older adults with lower extremity arthritis.

**Key Research Findings:**
• Land-based and water-based exercise both reduce pain and improve function in mild-to-moderate knee/hip OA (Cochrane review)
• Exercise therapy reduces pain, fatigue, and inflammatory biomarkers in both RA and OA (2025 meta-review in Frontiers in Physiology)
• Benefits extend beyond symptoms: improved cardiovascular health, mental health, sleep quality, and overall functional capacity
• Individualized, structured programs tailored to specific joints and limitations are most effective
• Adherence is the primary challenge — supervised programs show better outcomes than unsupervised

**What This Means for an App:**
The science strongly supports an exercise-based intervention. The key challenge isn't whether exercise works (it does), but whether an app can drive adherence and deliver appropriately individualized programs. An app that covers ROM, strengthening, and gentle aerobic exercises, personalized by affected joints, with progression tracking, has strong clinical grounding.
highlights: Exercise is ACR-recommended first-line treatment for OA and RA — stronger recommendation than many drugs
Quadriceps strengthening: 0.32 effect size for pain reduction and function improvement
Four pillars: range of motion (daily), strengthening (2-3x/week), aerobic (150 min/week), aquatic
Tai Chi strongly recommended by ACR specifically for knee/hip OA
Adherence is the #1 challenge — supervised programs outperform unsupervised
Individualized programs tailored to specific joints are most effective

sections.title: Key Features an Arthritis Exercise App Should Have
sections.content:
Based on competitive gaps, clinical evidence, and user needs for older adults with arthritis, here are the essential and differentiating features:

**ESSENTIAL (Must-Have for MVP):**

1. Joint-Specific Exercise Library — Exercises organized by affected joint (knee, hip, shoulder, hand/wrist, neck, ankle, elbow) and arthritis type (OA vs RA). Video demonstrations with clear, slow-paced instruction. This is the #1 gap in consumer apps.

2. Pain Level Tracking — Pre- and post-exercise pain rating (simple 0-10 scale or smiley faces). Track pain by joint over time. Morning stiffness duration tracking. Flare day detection to auto-adjust recommendations.

3. Adaptive Difficulty — Exercise intensity adjusts based on reported pain, progress, and flare status. On bad days, app should suggest gentler ROM exercises. On good days, progress to strengthening. This mimics what a good PT does.

4. Daily Exercise Routines — Curated 10-20 minute routines (matching Kaia's 10-15 min sweet spot). Morning stiffness routine, strengthening routine, gentle/flare day routine. Users shouldn't have to think about what to do.

5. Progress Tracking & Visualization — Weekly/monthly views of pain levels, exercise completion, mobility improvements. Streak tracking for motivation. Shareable reports for doctor visits (addressing MyRA's limitation).

6. Reminders & Scheduling — Customizable daily reminders. Medication reminder integration. Appointment reminders.

**DIFFERENTIATING (V2+):**

7. Pose Estimation & Form Correction — Camera-based real-time feedback on exercise form using MediaPipe or Apple Vision. Kaia Health proved this works on smartphones and matches PT-level feedback. Rep counting, range of motion measurement, safety alerts for dangerous form.

8. PT/Provider Connection — Ability to share progress reports and exercise videos with physical therapist. Async feedback from PT on form. This bridges the gap between fully autonomous apps and expensive PT platforms.

9. Personalized Program Generation — AI-driven program creation based on intake assessment (which joints, severity, goals, fitness level, equipment available). Progressive overload scheduling.

10. Community & Education — Peer support groups. Educational content about arthritis management. Arthritis Foundation content integration.

11. Wearable Integration — Apple Watch, Fitbit for activity tracking, heart rate during exercise, step counting. Import data rather than requiring manual entry.

12. Flare Management Protocol — When user reports a flare, app shifts to gentle ROM, icing guidance, and rest recommendations. Tracks flare frequency and potential triggers.
highlights: Joint-specific exercise library with video demos is the #1 competitive gap to fill
10-20 minute daily routines — clinically validated duration, matches Kaia's sweet spot
Adaptive difficulty based on pain/flare status mimics what a good PT does
Pose estimation proven viable on smartphones by Kaia Health's Motion Coach
Shareable doctor reports address a key limitation of existing consumer apps
Flare management protocol is a unique differentiator no consumer app offers

sections.title: Technology Considerations
sections.content:
**Pose Estimation Options:**

• MediaPipe (Google) — Best cross-platform option. Open-source, runs entirely on-device (privacy-preserving), tracks 33 body landmarks in real time. Proven in production by Kaia Health for exercise form correction in MSK patients. Works on standard smartphones with no additional hardware. Supports iOS and Android. Active development with 2026 updates. QuickPose SDK provides production-ready wrapper for faster integration.

• Apple Vision Framework — iOS-only alternative with better depth perception when paired with TrueDepth camera. Better for face/hand tracking specifically. Consider as iOS enhancement layer on top of MediaPipe for cross-platform base.

• Approach: Start without pose estimation in MVP (video-guided only). Add MediaPipe-based form feedback in V2. This is validated by Kaia's trajectory — they launched with exercise videos, added Motion Coach later.

**Rep Counting & Form Correction:**
• MediaPipe landmarks enable joint angle calculation (e.g., knee flexion angle during squats)
• Define safe ROM ranges per exercise, alert when user exceeds or under-performs
• Rep counting via peak detection on joint angle time series
• Latency must be <100ms for real-time feedback to feel responsive

**Accessibility for Older Users (Critical):**
• 3-tap navigation rule — validated in gerontechnology research. No feature should be more than 3 taps from home screen
• Minimum 16pt font, high contrast mode, large touch targets (minimum 44x44pt per Apple HIG)
• Voice guidance during exercises so users don't need to watch screen while moving
• Avoid virtual keyboards where possible — use sliders, pickers, large buttons
• Simple onboarding — no account creation required to start. Email/password optional.
• Support for Dynamic Type (iOS) and font scaling (Android)
• Haptic feedback for exercise transitions
• Consider that users may have hand arthritis — avoid pinch/zoom, small buttons, or precise gestures

**Offline Support:**
• Exercise videos must be downloadable for offline use. Many older adults have unreliable internet or use Wi-Fi only.
• Core exercise tracking should work fully offline with sync when connected
• Use progressive download — cache the user's current week of exercises

**Tech Stack Recommendation:**
• React Native or Flutter for cross-platform (iOS + Android) with native modules for camera/pose estimation
• Alternative: Swift/Kotlin native for best camera and pose estimation performance, but doubles development effort
• SQLite or Realm for offline-first local data storage
• Simple cloud sync (Firebase/Supabase) for backup and doctor sharing
• Video hosting: pre-recorded exercise videos (not live streaming) to minimize bandwidth
• Consider starting iOS-first given Apple's stronger accessibility framework and older adult adoption (iPhone users 65+ are growing fastest demographic)
highlights: MediaPipe: best cross-platform pose estimation, proven by Kaia Health for MSK exercise correction
Start MVP without pose estimation (video-guided), add form correction in V2
3-tap navigation rule is validated for older adult app design
Voice guidance during exercises critical — users can't watch screen while moving
Hand arthritis consideration: avoid small buttons, pinch gestures, virtual keyboards
Offline-first architecture essential — exercise videos must be downloadable
iOS-first may be optimal given 65+ demographic iPhone adoption trends

sections.title: Market Opportunity
sections.content:
**Arthritis Prevalence:**
• 53.2 million Americans have doctor-diagnosed arthritis (CDC)
• Women disproportionately affected: 20.9% vs 16.3% of men
• 88% of OA patients are 45+ years old; 43% are 65+
• Arthritis is the #1 cause of disability in the US
• Global OA prevalence exceeds 500 million people

**Market Size:**
• Arthritic therapeutics market: $77 billion globally in 2026 (6.3% CAGR)
• Osteoarthritis therapeutics specifically: $11.85 billion in 2026, growing to $24.52 billion by 2034
• Digital MSK care market: $5.10 billion in 2025, growing to $15.92 billion by 2032 (17.6% CAGR)
• The digital MSK segment is growing 3x faster than the overall arthritis market

**Key Players Revenue:**
• Hinge Health: $732M projected 2026 revenue (51% YoY growth)
• Sword Health: $3B valuation, acquired Kaia for $285M
• Combined Hinge + Sword cover 100M+ eligible lives through employers

**The Gap — Direct-to-Consumer:**
• Enterprise platforms (Hinge, Sword, Omada) are employer-funded and inaccessible to most individuals
• Estimated 80%+ of arthritis patients do NOT have access through their employer
• Self-pay digital health willingness varies by age and health status, but chronic pain patients show highest willingness to pay
• HSA/FSA eligibility: Digital therapeutics with clinical evidence can qualify. IRS Letter Ruling allows HSA payments for apps prescribed by a doctor. This is a growth area.

**Demographics & User Profile (Your Mom's Cohort):**
• Primary target: Women 55-75 with OA of knee, hip, or hands
• This demographic is increasingly smartphone-literate (76% of 65+ own smartphones in 2026)
• They prefer guided, structured programs over open-ended exercise libraries
• Price sensitivity: willing to pay $5-15/month for a health app that demonstrably helps, but free tier is critical for trial
• Trust signals matter: PT-designed content, medical advisory board, Arthritis Foundation alignment

**Insurance/HSA Opportunity:**
• Growing trend of insurers covering digital therapeutics
• Apps with clinical evidence and FDA registration can access reimbursement pathways
• HSA/FSA eligibility is a strong selling point for this demographic
• Long-term play: if the app demonstrates outcomes, approach employers/insurers as a B2B2C channel
highlights: 53.2 million Americans with arthritis — #1 cause of disability in the US
Digital MSK market growing at 17.6% CAGR — 3x faster than overall arthritis therapeutics
80%+ of arthritis patients lack employer-sponsored digital MSK access — massive gap
Target demographic (women 55-75): 76% smartphone ownership, willing to pay $5-15/mo
HSA/FSA eligibility possible for clinically-backed digital therapeutics
Hinge Health alone projecting $732M in 2026 — proves the demand exists

sections.content:

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Target** | Employer-sponsored MSK | Employer-sponsored MSK | OA self-management | RA symptom tracking | All arthritis types | Chronic pain (general) |
| **Pricing** | Free via employer (B2B) | Free via employer (B2B) | Free + premium | Free | Free | Free + $9.99/mo premium |
| **Exercise Videos** | Yes, PT-designed, adaptive | Yes, AI-guided with Motion Coach | Basic tutorials | No exercises | Modifications only | Breathing/visualization |

| **Pain Tracking** | Yes | Yes | Yes (detailed) | Yes (by activity) | No | Yes |
| **Joint-Specific Programs** | Yes (all major joints) | Yes (all major joints) | Knee/hip focus | RA joints | Customizable | No |
| **Doctor/PT Sharing** | Built-in PT access | Built-in coaching | Yes | No (major limitation) | No | No |
| **Personalization** | High (PT + AI) | High (AI-driven) | Moderate | Low | Moderate | Low |
| **App Store Rating** | 4.8 iOS / 4.6 Android | 4.7 iOS / 4.5 Android | 5.0 iOS / 5.0 Android | 3.8 iOS | N/A (web-based) | 4.8 iOS / 4.7 Android |

**Key Takeaway:** The two clinically superior products (Hinge, Sword) are inaccessible to self-paying individuals. The consumer apps that ARE accessible (Jointfully, MyRA, YES) lack video exercise guidance, pose estimation, form correction, and meaningful personalization. This is the opportunity.
highlights: Hinge and Sword are clinically excellent but employer-gated — no self-pay option
Jointfully is highest-rated consumer app (5/5) but lacks video guidance and AI features
Only Kaia (now Sword) offers smartphone-based pose estimation for exercise correction
MyRA's biggest limitation: cannot share reports with healthcare providers
No consumer arthritis app combines exercise videos + form correction + pain tracking + personalization
The white space: clinical-quality exercise guidance accessible to self-paying individuals

sections.title: MVP Recommendation — What V1 Should Look Like
sections.content:
**The Core Insight:** Your mom doesn't need a $3B platform. She needs a simple app that tells her exactly what exercises to do today, shows her how to do them safely, tracks her pain, and adapts when she's having a bad day. No existing consumer app does this well.

**V1 MVP — 'Arthritis Exercise Companion'**

**Onboarding (2 minutes max):**
• Which joints bother you? (tap to select on body diagram: knees, hips, shoulders, hands, neck, ankles, etc.)
• How would you rate your pain today? (simple slider)
• What's your current activity level? (sedentary / somewhat active / active)
• Any exercises your PT has recommended? (optional)
• No account creation required to start using the app

**Daily Experience:**
• Open app → see today's routine (10-15 minutes)
• Each exercise has a clear video demonstration with a calm, slow-paced voiceover
• Large text showing: exercise name, reps/duration, which joint it helps, modifications for bad days
• Voice guidance so user can listen without watching screen while exercising
• After routine: rate your pain (quick slider), log any notes
• Streak counter and gentle encouragement (not gamified — this demographic responds to health outcomes, not points)

**Exercise Content (Phase 1 — 60-80 exercises):**
• Morning stiffness routine (ROM focused, 5-10 min)
• Knee program (ROM + quad/hamstring strengthening)
• Hip program (ROM + hip flexor/glute strengthening)
• Hand/wrist program (ROM + grip strengthening)
• Shoulder program (ROM + rotator cuff)
• Gentle full-body (seated exercises, chair yoga)
• Flare day routine (very gentle ROM only)
• Each exercise filmed from multiple angles, with modification for easier/harder versions

**Pain & Progress Dashboard:**
• Weekly pain trend chart per joint
• Exercise completion calendar
• 'Share with my doctor' — export PDF summary of last 30 days
• Morning stiffness duration tracking

**What V1 Does NOT Include (Save for V2+):**
• No pose estimation or camera features (add in V2 once core experience is validated)
• No AI-generated programs (curate manually with PT input first)
• No social features or community
• No wearable integration
• No live PT access

**Monetization:**
• Free tier: 1 joint program + pain tracking + 3 exercises/day
• Premium: $7.99/month or $59.99/year — all joints, unlimited exercises, doctor reports, flare protocols
• Position for HSA/FSA eligibility in future with clinical validation

**Development Estimate:**
• iOS-first (React Native for future Android expansion)
• 60-80 exercise videos (hire a PT to film, budget $3-5K)
• Core app development: 8-12 weeks for a small team
• Medical review: have a rheumatologist or PT review all content before launch

**Success Metrics:**
• Primary: weekly active users completing 3+ exercise sessions
• Secondary: pain score improvement over 30 days
• Tertiary: premium conversion rate

**Why This Wins:**
It's the first consumer arthritis app that combines PT-quality video exercise guidance, joint-specific personalization, adaptive difficulty based on pain/flare status, and doctor-shareable progress reports — at $7.99/month instead of requiring employer sponsorship. It fills the exact gap between $732M enterprise platforms and basic free apps with static images.
highlights: MVP: joint-specific video exercises + pain tracking + adaptive daily routines
10-15 minute daily routines with voice guidance — validated duration and format
Onboarding in 2 minutes: select joints, rate pain, set activity level — no account required
Free tier (1 joint) + premium at $7.99/mo or $59.99/yr — positioned for HSA/FSA
60-80 exercises filmed with PT, ~$3-5K video production budget
Skip pose estimation in V1 — validate core experience first, add camera features in V2
Key differentiator: clinical-quality guidance at consumer price, not employer-gated

outlook.summary: The arthritis exercise app market has a massive underserved segment: the 80%+ of arthritis patients without employer-sponsored digital MSK access. Enterprise platforms (Hinge Health, Sword Health) have proven that digital exercise therapy works and people will use it, but they've left consumer self-pay wide open. A focused MVP offering PT-quality video exercise guidance, joint-specific personalization, pain tracking, and adaptive daily routines can capture this gap at $7.99/month. The technology is proven (Kaia validated smartphone pose estimation), the clinical evidence is strong (ACR recommends exercise as first-line treatment), and the demographics are favorable (53M Americans, growing smartphone adoption in 65+). Start simple, validate with real users like your mom, and layer on AI/pose estimation in V2.

Digital MSK market growing 17.6% CAGR — $5.1B to $15.9B by 2032

Kaia Health proved smartphone pose estimation works for MSK — technology is validated
No consumer app combines video exercises + personalization + pain tracking + doctor sharing
HSA/FSA eligibility pathway provides monetization upside beyond subscriptions
bearish: Hinge Health or Sword could launch a self-pay consumer tier and instantly dominate
Exercise adherence is the #1 challenge — apps without human coaching show lower retention
Older adult app adoption still has friction despite improving smartphone literacy
Gartner: 40%+ of agentic AI health projects scrapped — digital health has high failure rates
Clinical validation takes time and money — without it, hard to differentiate from generic fitness apps
